messages:
neha: Quick idea — can we add a deploy alias + pinfile template to cut down manual pin churn during canaries? Right now folks run `/deploy canary --service foo --version v2` then forget to pin the rollout. I'd love a shorthand or repo-level pins.yaml that the bot reads.

sam: +1. We've been reinventing this across services. Two parts: (1) bot command alias like `/deploy pin` or `/deploy from-pin` and (2) a small pins.yaml we check into infra/ or repo root.

marta: Sketched a tiny pins.yaml that should be backward compatible. Thoughts?

```yaml
# pins.yaml - optional, bot autodetects repo root or infra/pins.yaml
pinned_services:
  - name: frontend
    version: v2.1.0
    reason: "stability baseline"
  - name: model-serving
    version: v2026-03-18
    reason: "canary pinned after perf tests"
metadata:
  author: marta
  updated: 2026-03-18
```

jay: Nice. For the bot I propose these behaviors:
- if pins.yaml exists, `/deploy canary --use-pins` will auto-apply pins after a successful canary run
- `/deploy pin <service> <version>` creates/updates pins.yaml (with dry-run flag)
- support a `--announce` flag so the bot appends a short note to release notes and adds a pinned tag to rollout metadata

neha: Also: include an escape hatch for rollbacks — if a canary fails, bot should 1) annotate the release with rollback reason, 2) optionally auto-rollback pinned services to prior version, and 3) open a rollback retro thread link. Example command: `/deploy rollback --service model-serving --to v2026-03-01 --reason "perf regression"`

sam: Edge cases: what if pins.yaml pins a version that isn't compatible with dependent services? We should add a quick preflight validation step that runs `compat-check` (a lightweight script) and refuses the pin if it fails, or at least warns and requires `--force`. Also respect change windows for production.

neha: Change window idea: bot checks a service-level change_window in pins.yaml or repo config and refuses schedule outside that unless `--override-window`. Example schedule flow: `/deploy schedule --service frontend --window "2026-03-21 03:00-04:00" --use-pins`

marta: Updated pins.yaml proposal to include optional change_window and preflight hooks: 

```yaml
pinned_services:
  - name: frontend
    version: v2.1.0
    change_window: "wed-03:00-05:00"
    preflight: "scripts/preflight/frontend-check.sh"
```

jay: I'll PR the bot changes: alias support, `--use-pins` flag, pins.yaml resolver (repo root -> infra/ -> deploy/), and an opt-in automatic release-note annotation. PR will include a small e2e that simulates canary -> pin -> schedule -> rollback. Opening now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/deploy-bot/pull/472 (WIP)

deploy-bot: I ran a quick dry-run on the `pins.yaml` snippet above. Detected 2 services, validated YAML schema, no compat-check run (dry-run). To test preflight, run: `/deploy preflight --service frontend --script scripts/preflight/frontend-check.sh`

neha: Love it — can we also add a short template for release notes that bot appends when pin happens? e.g., `Pinned model-serving -> v2026-03-18 (reason: perf stable)` so product and support get notified.

sam: yes — bot should add an `#pins` block in the release notes. Minimal format so changelog tools can parse it.

marta: LGTM. Minor nit: prefer `pins.yaml` name exactly (no pins.yml variants) to reduce detection complexity.

jay: I'll include lint and a small migrator that converts existing manual pins into pins.yaml when PRer runs.

neha: Great. I'll try this flow in staging tomorrow during the dev cluster window and report back. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Reminder: test cluster command available — `/deploy dry-run --use-pins --cluster=dev`.
